question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

 

The librarian arranged all the books on the new shelf.
option_1: All the books were arranged on the new shelf by the librarian.
option_2: All the books arranged on the new shelf by the librarian.
option_3: All the books are arranged on the new shelf by the librarian.
option_4: All the books were arranging on the new shelf by the librarian.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. All the books were arranged on the new shelf by the librarian.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The object of the active sentence, "all the books," becomes the subject of the passive sentence, and the verb takes the form "was/were + past participle": "arranged" becomes "were arranged", matching the plural subject.

◦ Complete sentence: All the books were arranged on the new shelf by the librarian.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "...arranged on the new shelf..." — the auxiliary "were" is missing; the passive verb must be "were arranged".

 

• Option 3: "...are arranged..." — the present tense is wrongly used instead of the simple past "were arranged".

 

• Option 4: "...were arranging..." — the continuous form is wrongly used instead of the simple passive "were arranged".

 

NOTE

 

• The workers repaired the fence. → the fence was repaired by the workers (simple past active → simple past passive).

question:

option_1: The vendor sold fresh vegetables every morning.
option_2: The vendor sells fresh vegetables every morning.
option_3: The vendor is selling fresh vegetables every morning.
option_4: The vendor have sold fresh vegetables every morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The vendor sells fresh vegetables every morning.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The agent of the passive sentence, "the vendor," becomes the subject, and the passive verb "are sold" (simple present) converts to the active simple present "sells", agreeing with the singular subject.

◦ Complete sentence: The vendor sells fresh vegetables every morning.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "...sold fresh vegetables..." — the simple past is wrongly used instead of the simple present "sells".

 

• Option 3: "...is selling fresh vegetables..." — the continuous form is wrongly used instead of the simple present "sells".

 

• Option 4: "...have sold fresh vegetables..." — the present perfect is wrongly used, and it also fails to agree with the singular subject "the vendor".

 

NOTE

 

• Newspapers are delivered by the boy every day. → the boy delivers newspapers every day (simple present passive → simple present active).

question:

option_2: Every prescription must been verified carefully by the pharmacist.
option_3: Every prescription is must verified carefully by the pharmacist.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Every prescription must be verified carefully by the pharmacist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• With the modal "must", the passive form is "must be + past participle": "must be verified".

◦ Complete sentence: Every prescription must be verified carefully by the pharmacist.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "must been verified" — the incorrect form "must been" is used instead of "must be".

 

• Option 3: "is must verified" — this is an ungrammatical construction; a modal cannot be preceded by "is".

 

• Option 4: "must have verified" — this wrongly forms a perfect modal instead of the simple modal passive "must be verified".

• The technician must inspect every machine daily. → every machine must be inspected daily by the technician (modal "must" + base verb → "must be" + past participle).

question: Select the option that is expressed in passive voice.
option_1: The children are playing cricket in the park.
option_2: The cake was baked by my grandmother.
option_3: She has completed her assignment on time.
option_4: They will visit the museum tomorrow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The cake was baked by my grandmother.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A sentence is in the passive voice when its subject receives the action rather than performing it, typically formed with "be + past participle". Only "The cake was baked by my grandmother" fits this structure.

◦ The cake was baked by my grandmother — is in the passive voice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "The children are playing cricket..." — this is in the active voice; the subject "the children" performs the action.

 

• Option 3: "She has completed her assignment..." — this is in the active voice; the subject "she" performs the action.

 

• Option 4: "They will visit the museum..." — this is in the active voice; the subject "they" performs the action.

 

NOTE

 

• Identify the passive sentence among: "He cooked dinner." / "Dinner was cooked by him." → "Dinner was cooked by him." (subject receives the action, formed with "be" + past participle).

• Option 1: "Doesn't every expense report approved...?" — the auxiliary "Doesn't" cannot combine with a past participle; the correct form is "Isn't...approved?".

 

• Option 2: "Is every expense report not approve...?" — the base form "approve" is wrongly used instead of the past participle "approved".

 

• Option 4: "Wasn't every expense report approved...?" — the past tense is wrongly used instead of the present tense "Isn't...approved".

 

NOTE

 

• Doesn't the chef prepare every dish personally? → Isn't every dish prepared personally by the chef? (negative simple present interrogative active → passive).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

 

Why did the referee stop the match abruptly?
option_1: Why is the match stopped abruptly by the referee?
option_2: Why did the match stopped abruptly by the referee?
option_3: Why the match was stopped abruptly by the referee?
option_4: Why was the match stopped abruptly by the referee?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Why was the match stopped abruptly by the referee?.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A wh-question in the simple past ("Why did...stop?") converts to the passive form "Why was + subject + past participle?": "Why was the match stopped?"

◦ Complete sentence: Why was the match stopped abruptly by the referee?

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Why is the match stopped...?" — the present tense is wrongly used instead of the past tense "was stopped".

 

• Option 2: "Why did the match stopped...?" — the auxiliary "did" cannot combine with a past participle in this way; the correct form is "was stopped".

 

• Option 3: "Why the match was stopped...?" — the interrogative word order is broken; "was" must come immediately after "why".

 

NOTE

 

• Why did the officer reject the application? → Why was the application rejected by the officer? (wh-question in the simple past, active → passive).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

 

One must respect the traditions of every culture.
option_1: The traditions of every culture must be respected.
option_2: The traditions of every culture must be respect by one.
option_3: The traditions of every culture must respected.
option_4: The traditions of every culture must have been respected.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The traditions of every culture must be respected.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When the subject is the generic pronoun "one," the agent phrase "by one" is usually dropped in the passive, since it adds no real information.

◦ Complete sentence: The traditions of every culture must be respected.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "...must be respect by one." — the base form "respect" is wrongly used instead of the past participle "respected"; besides, retaining "by one" here is unnecessary since the agent is a generic pronoun.

 

• Option 3: "...must respected." — the auxiliary "be" is missing; the correct form is "must be respected".

 

• Option 4: "...must have been respected." — this wrongly adds the perfect aspect, which is not present in the original modal statement.

 

NOTE

 

• One should always keep one's promises. → promises should always be kept (generic pronoun "one" dropped in the passive).
